explanation: That's right. People who sort through open municipal dumps to find reusable items often run into discarded needles and toxic waste without any protective gear.

question: Which of these directly makes the heart muscle demand more oxygen?

options.A: A decreased force of heart contraction
options.B: An increased heart rate
options.C: A lower blood pressure reading
options.D: Relaxation of the coronary arteries

explanation: When the heart beats faster, it pumps more and works harder, which means it burns through a lot more oxygen. Makes total sense when you picture it!

question: Why does a tracheostomy tube have a removable inner cannula?

options.A: It allows easy cleaning and removal of dried mucus
options.B: It acts as a backup if the patient stops breathing
options.C: It measures the exact pressure in the lungs
options.D: It allows the patient to talk without a valve

explanation: Mucus builds up fast! The inner cannula can be easily taken out and cleaned so the airway stays open and clear.

question: How do standard daily contraceptive pills primarily prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By permanently blocking the fallopian tubes with scar tissue
options.B: By stopping ovulation and changing the cervical mucus
options.C: By killing all bacteria inside the vaginal canal
options.D: By neutralizing stomach acid so hormones cannot absorb

explanation: The hormones in the pill do a double-duty job: they tell the body to pause ovulation and make the cervical mucus thick so sperm can't get through.

question: Why shouldn't you try to push a protruding bone back under the skin during emergency care?

options.A: It can damage surrounding blood vessels and nerves and introduce deep infection.
options.B: It causes immediate paralysis of the entire central nervous system.
options.C: It makes it impossible for the doctor to take a clear X-ray later.
options.D: It automatically guarantees that the bone will never heal properly.

explanation: Pushing it back in can accidentally slice major blood vessels or nerves, and drag surface germs deep inside the sterile bone. Always leave bone repositioning to the medical team!

question: Which vital sign change usually comes with a widespread inflammatory response?

options.A: Elevated blood oxygen
options.B: Decreased heart rate
options.C: Elevated temperature
options.D: Lowered respiratory rate

explanation: Correct! Fever is a classic full-body response triggered when inflammatory signals talk to the brain's temperature control center.

question: Which common side effect of oral iron often scares patients, even though it's harmless?

options.A: Temporary hair thinning
options.B: Excessive saliva production
options.C: Bright yellow urine coloration
options.D: Dark or black-colored stools

explanation: Don't panic your patients! Unabsorbed iron turns stools dark or black, and it's a totally normal, harmless side effect.

question: Where does the hidden majority of sodium in our diets usually come from?

options.A: Hidden additives inside manufactured packaged foods
options.B: Natural spring water consumed throughout the day
options.C: Fresh vegetables grown in mineral-rich soil
options.D: The table salt shaker used right before eating

explanation: Correct! Most of our salt doesn't come from the shaker; it's already tucked away inside processed and packaged foods as a preservative.

question: Why is it so important to check lab results alongside a physical assessment rather than trusting the numbers alone?

options.A: Because physical assessments replace the need for serial blood draws
options.B: Because doctors do not review lab values unless symptoms are documented
options.C: Because clinical symptoms show how the patient is tolerating the physiological shift
options.D: Because laboratory printers frequently lose patient identification data

explanation: Two patients might have the exact same lab result, but one might feel fine while the other is crashing. Always nurse the patient, not just the lab paper!

question: Why is running low on folate (folic acid) especially risky in early pregnancy?

options.A: It impairs rapid cell division and increases the risk of neural tube defects
options.B: It stops the placenta from attaching to the uterine wall entirely
options.C: It causes immediate destruction of all maternal white blood cells
options.D: It directly causes sudden maternal hemorrhage during the first month

explanation: Folate is a builder's best friend for DNA and fast-multiplying cells! Without enough in early pregnancy, the baby's brain and spinal cord (neural tube) can fail to develop properly. That's why routine folic acid is a must.

question: What is the main goal of secondary stroke prevention strategies?

options.A: To prevent a recurrent stroke by managing underlying risk factors
options.B: To eliminate the need for any ongoing physical therapy
options.C: To reverse existing brain cell death and restore lost tissue
options.D: To cure the underlying genetic cause of high blood pressure

explanation: Brilliant! Secondary prevention is all about keeping lifestyle habits in check, taking medications properly, and managing blood pressure to stop another stroke from happening.

question: What is a common medical risk factor that makes a patient bleed more easily?

options.A: Taking anticoagulant medications
options.B: Eating a diet high in leafy green vegetables
options.C: Engaging in regular light aerobic exercise
options.D: Having high levels of dietary iron

explanation: Anticoagulants slow down the body's clotting process, making it much harder for bleeding to stop once it starts. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is the immediate priority when caring for a patient who has just suffered a severe burn injury?

options.A: Applying antibiotic ointment to all blistered areas
options.B: Calculating the total body surface area burned
options.C: Inserting a large-bore intravenous line for pain meds
options.D: Securing the airway and assessing breathing

explanation: Airway stability always comes first in trauma and burn management because smoke inhalation or laryngeal edema can quickly cause suffocation. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h6)

question: What is the main difference between an early marriage and a forced marriage?

options.A: Forced marriage involves financial payment, while early marriage involves religious rites.
options.B: Forced marriage only happens to adults, while early marriage only happens to children.
options.C: Early marriage is legally recognized worldwide, whereas forced marriage is always illegal.
options.D: Early marriage is based on age, while forced marriage lacks free and full consent from at least one party.

explanation: Spot on! Early marriage focuses primarily on the person's young age, while forced marriage happens when someone is pushed into it without their true, free consent.

question: Why must a nurse check the pulse and skin color below a fractured limb?

options.A: To check for signs of blood vessel or nerve damage
options.B: To calculate the exact date when the bone will heal
options.C: To prevent the development of a systemic bone infection
options.D: To determine how much calcium the patient's body needs

explanation: Swelling or displaced bone fragments can pinch nearby arteries and nerves, cutting off blood supply and sensation to the fingers or toes. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h3)

question: What must form first before a bone can grow using endochondral ossification?

options.A: Primary vascular plexus
options.B: Hyaline cartilage model
options.C: Dense collagenous tendon
options.D: Fibrous connective tissue sheet

explanation: Think of cartilage as a tiny practice sculpture! Endochondral bones need a hyaline cartilage model first, which is later replaced by true bone.

question: How can rude or harsh behavior by staff at a receiving hospital negatively affect the referral system?

options.A: It discourages patients and their relatives from seeking formal care in the future
options.B: It improves communication between traditional healers and doctors
options.C: It makes patients recover faster because they want to leave early
options.D: It encourages villagers to build more primary health care centers

explanation: Negative attitudes create a hostile environment, causing patients to avoid hospitals and patronize unqualified providers instead. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h7)

question: Why must safety measures respect a patient's independence?

options.A: Patients will ignore rules that make them feel helpless
options.B: Families prefer not to assist elderly relatives
options.C: Independent patients recover faster from surgery
options.D: Hospital policies demand self-care routines

explanation: If safety rules take away all freedom, patients often try to bypass them secretly, which actually increases their risk of accidents. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h1)

question: How does severe malnutrition affect drugs that normally bind strongly to albumin?

options.A: It increases free, active drug in the blood, raising toxicity risk
options.B: It forces the drug to store permanently in bone marrow
options.C: It makes the blood-brain barrier open to everything
options.D: It causes the liver to destroy the medicine immediately

explanation: Without enough albumin (due to poor nutrition), there are fewer taxi cabs for the drug. This leaves too much free medicine floating around, which can lead to accidental overdose.

question: Which behavioral change is a classic warning sign of potential substance abuse?

options.A: Neglecting work or school responsibilities
options.B: Consistent weight gain and healthy skin tone
options.C: An increased interest in family activities
options.D: Sudden improvement in daily sleep routines

explanation: Correct! When substances take center stage in someone's life, important commitments like classes, work, and family duties usually start slipping away.

question: What is the first step when preparing to share serious news using the SPIKES protocol?

options.A: Setting up a private, quiet space with minimal interruptions
options.B: Giving the patient all test results immediately upon entering
options.C: Asking the family to leave the room for privacy
options.D: Reading the patient's vital signs out loud

explanation: The first step of SPIKES focuses on setting, which involves arranging a private, comfortable environment for the discussion. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h4)

question: Why can unsafe formula feeding sometimes pose an even greater danger to an infant than HIV?

options.A: Contaminated water and dirty bottles cause fatal diarrhea and severe malnutrition
options.B: Commercial formula lacks basic calories needed for normal brain growth
options.C: Babies fed with formula develop immediate resistance to routine vaccines
options.D: Prepared formula breaks down the infant immune system faster than the virus

explanation: Where clean water isn't guaranteed, bad hygiene around formula bottles can cause severe tummy bugs that put a baby's life at serious risk.

question: Why is community health nursing so important to primary health care in Nigeria?

options.A: It manages all tertiary hospital admissions across the country
options.B: It brings preventative and basic health services directly to local populations
options.C: It exclusively handles complex surgical procedures in rural areas
options.D: It replaces the need for doctors in government hospitals

explanation: You got it! By stepping into local clinics, schools, and homes, community health nurses make sure everyday preventative care actually reaches where people live.

question: Which of these best describes an unsafe injection practice?

options.A: Giving an intramuscular shot without asking the patient's age first
options.B: Any injection action that puts patients or staff at risk of preventable harm
options.C: Using a plastic syringe instead of a glass one
options.D: Giving an injection past normal visiting hours

explanation: If it puts anyone at risk of harm through contamination, reuse, or bad handling, it's unsafe. Trust your gut—if it feels risky, it probably is!

question: Why is a laryngoscopy done?

options.A: It takes X-rays of the chest and inflates collapsed lung tissue simultaneously.
options.B: It measures blood pressure in the throat and delivers emergency oral medications.
options.C: It cures chronic lung infections and removes foreign bodies from the stomach.
options.D: It checks voice box issues and also helps place breathing tubes during resuscitation.

explanation: Exactly! It's a handy tool both for figuring out throat problems and for guiding breathing tubes when someone needs emergency help.

question: What is a pathologic fracture?

options.A: A break occurring in a bone weakened by an underlying disease
options.B: A minor hairline crack caused by repetitive athletic training
options.C: A clean break resulting from a high-speed motor vehicle crash
options.D: A fracture caused strictly by a direct blow from a blunt object

explanation: Pathologic fractures happen because an existing disease like cancer or osteoporosis has already made the bone fragile. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h2)

question: How do peptide and protein hormones typically travel through the bloodstream?

options.A: They require specialized carrier proteins to move through blood
options.B: They precipitate out of solution if not bound to electrolytes
options.C: They are water-soluble and dissolve freely in blood plasma
options.D: They are fat-soluble and travel inside red blood cells

explanation: Because protein and peptide hormones love water, they dissolve easily right into the watery plasma of your blood and swim along freely without needing a special ride.

question: What is the primary focus of pharmacogenetics?

options.A: How genetic differences affect drug responses
options.B: How manufacturing plants create generic drugs
options.C: How bacteria develop resistance to antibiotics
options.D: How the human body excretes dietary proteins

explanation: Pharmacogenetics specifically studies how a person's inherited genetic makeup alters the way their body handles and responds to medications. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T5#GNS125_U1_T5_h1)

question: A pregnant woman at 36 weeks comes in with a fully infibulated Type III FGM scar. What is the best clinical approach?

options.A: Advise her to deliver completely unassisted at home
options.B: Plan for an antenatal or intrapartum defibulation procedure
options.C: Wait until pushing begins without any clinical preparation
options.D: Perform an immediate emergency hysterectomy

explanation: You nailed it! Planning ahead for defibulation lets the birth canal open safely before or during labor, preventing severe tears and fetal distress. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h6)

question: Where is laboratory research typically carried out?

options.A: In busy hospital waiting rooms
options.B: During community health outreach
options.C: Inside patients' private homes
options.D: In a controlled, artificial setting

explanation: Correct! Lab research takes place in controlled environments where scientists can carefully manage and manipulate variables. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the main reason we give antibiotic eye ointment to a newborn right after birth?

options.A: Lubricating dry eyes caused by bright delivery lights
options.B: Preventing ophthalmia neonatorum from birth canal infections
options.C: Treating congenital cataracts and visual impairments
options.D: Preventing viral conjunctivitis acquired from nursery staff

explanation: This routine ointment protects the baby's eyes from nasty bacteria like gonorrhea or chlamydia that they might pick up while passing through the birth canal.

question: What is a very common early emotional reaction after someone suddenly acquires a physical disability?

options.A: Complete indifference to their physical status
options.B: A grief response including denial and anger
options.C: Excitement about starting vocational training
options.D: Immediate acceptance and joyful adaptation

explanation: Losing body function is a heavy life blow. Feelings like shock, anger, and denial are completely normal parts of processing grief—be patient with your patients!

question: Why is the rectal route frequently used for pediatric fever management?

options.A: It avoids the struggle of forcing bitter syrups down a sick child's throat
options.B: Children absorb all medications ten times faster rectally than orally
options.C: Suppositories never melt prematurely in young children
options.D: It eliminates the need for any hand hygiene during administration

explanation: Infants and young children often spit out oral medications, so antipyretic suppositories provide a reliable alternative. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h5)

question: Who has the main responsibility for setting health rules that must be followed in a school?

options.A: The local police department
options.B: Enrolling students
options.C: Parent-teacher athletics committees
options.D: School management

explanation: Exactly! The school management team holds the authority required to create and enforce official health policies.

question: Why does Lassa fever spike during the dry season?

options.A: Farming activities and bush burning drive rats closer to homes
options.B: Cold weather lowers human immune systems significantly
options.C: Increased humidity allows the virus to spread faster in the air
options.D: Heavy rainfall causes stagnant water to breed the virus

explanation: When fields are cleared and burned, the rats lose their natural habitat and move straight into grain stores and residential areas.

question: Why do nurses use numbers in the GCS instead of writing words like 'drowsy' in the patient's chart?

options.A: Doctors are not trained to read standard English descriptions
options.B: Words take too much time to write in a busy hospital chart
options.C: Numbers are the only way to bill insurance companies for care
options.D: Numerical scores prevent misunderstandings between different staff members

explanation: Words like 'drowsy' can mean different things to different nurses. A number gives everyone a clear, shared picture so we can easily track if the patient is getting better or worse.

question: A nurse is teaching an outpatient about methimazole. Which instruction is the most important to emphasize before they leave?

options.A: Stop taking the medication as soon as your hand tremors stop
options.B: Avoid eating all green leafy vegetables while on this therapy
options.C: Report any yellowing of the eyes or dark urine immediately
options.D: Double your next dose if you happen to forget taking yesterday's pill

explanation: Spotting liver trouble early is life-saving! Yellow eyes (jaundice) or dark urine mean they need to call the clinic right away.

question: A patient tells you they plan to stop their blood pressure medication as soon as they feel better. What should you as a nurse do?

options.A: Agree that stopping is fine since the symptoms have temporarily disappeared
options.B: Suggest they sell the remaining pills to a neighbor with similar symptoms
options.C: Explain that chronic conditions require ongoing treatment and counsel them on adherence
options.D: Tell them to double the dose tomorrow to finish the medication faster

explanation: Brilliant nursing judgment! Chronic illnesses need continuous management, and patient education is our superpower as nurses.

question: As a bedside nurse, why are you considered right at the center of hospital waste management?

options.A: Nurses are the only staff members allowed to touch trash
options.B: Nurses are legally liable for the city waste trucks
options.C: Nurses generate waste during daily patient care activities
options.D: Hospital management forces nurses to pay for disposal bins

explanation: Spot on! Because we give direct patient care every day, we are the first ones to handle and discard medical materials.

question: What is the main difference between a medical emergency and a surgical emergency?

options.A: Surgical emergencies never involve internal bleeding
options.B: Medical emergencies always require immediate surgery
options.C: Medical emergencies only happen outside the hospital
options.D: Surgical emergencies usually require an operation to fix

explanation: You've got this! Surgical emergencies involve physical trauma or acute organ trouble that typically needs an operation to fix, while medical emergencies usually stem from internal illnesses. Think surgery vs. medicine!

question: Why is it so important to document a drug reaction in the notes and tell the patient about it?

options.A: To prevent the patient from receiving the same dangerous drug in the future
options.B: To satisfy legal insurance requirements for the nursing council
options.C: To prove to the doctor that the nurse made the correct diagnosis
options.D: To make sure the hospital pharmacy gets paid for the wasted medication

explanation: Clear records and patient education protect them from getting that same harmful drug again in future hospital visits.

question: What usually happens if a patient accidentally swallows a sublingual tablet with water?

options.A: The drug will turn into a toxic substance in the intestines.
options.B: The drug may be destroyed by stomach acid and liver enzymes.
options.C: There will be no change in how the drug works.
options.D: The drug will absorb twice as fast through the stomach lining.

explanation: Correct! Swallowing it means it faces stomach acid and the liver, which can weaken or destroy the drug before it works.

question: You are about to give oral digoxin, but your adult patient's apical pulse is 52 beats per minute. What should you do?

options.A: Withhold the dose and notify the prescriber
options.B: Encourage exercise to raise the pulse before giving it
options.C: Give half the dose now and half in six hours
options.D: Administer the medication as prescribed immediately

explanation: Brilliant clinical judgement! Always remember: if an adult patient's pulse is below 60, hold the digoxin and check in with the doctor to keep your patient safe from toxicity.

question: What do we mean by 'patient harm' in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Injury caused by medical care rather than the underlying disease
options.B: Emotional distress caused by a patient's personal family issues
options.C: Discomfort experienced before a formal diagnosis is made
options.D: Natural progression of a chronic illness over time

explanation: Spot on! Patient harm refers specifically to injuries that happen because of the medical care or treatment provided, rather than the natural course of the sickness itself. Keep up the great thinking!

question: What is the primary health benefit of a PTA providing a borehole in a school?

options.A: It lowers the electricity bills of the school
options.B: It provides mineral water for teachers to sell
options.C: It reduces the spread of waterborne diseases
options.D: It ensures students wash their uniforms daily

explanation: Clean and safe drinking water prevents dangerous waterborne infections such as typhoid and cholera among pupils. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h3)

question: You walk into a warm ward and notice a patient is shivering and moving very slowly. Which condition should pop into your head?

options.A: Diabetes mellitus
options.B: Cushing syndrome
options.C: Hyperthyroidism
options.D: Hypothyroidism

explanation: When the thyroid is underactive, internal heat production drops. That's why these patients often feel freezing cold and sluggish, even when everyone else is comfortable.

question: What is the most common cause of myocarditis?

options.A: Viruses
options.B: Fungi
options.C: Parasites
options.D: Prions

explanation: Viruses are the top culprits behind myocarditis worldwide, often attacking the heart muscle after a normal viral infection. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h3)

question: Where are community health nurses most likely to meet families to talk about the value of school?

options.A: Inside high courtrooms during child custody legal proceedings
options.B: During parliamentary budget planning sessions in the capital city
options.C: During home visits, immunization clinics, and community meetings
options.D: At international nursing research conferences held overseas

explanation: Spot on! Routine outreach gives nurses a great chance to chat directly with parents right where they live and gather.

question: How does showing empathy directly help a patient during a health consultation?

options.A: It replaces the need to prescribe any medications
options.B: It stops them from asking questions about the treatment
options.C: It guarantees that their illness will heal twice as fast
options.D: It makes them feel safe and understood, reducing their anxiety

explanation: Empathy validates the patient's feelings, which lowers stress and builds the trust needed for an honest health assessment. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T12#GNS124_U5_T12_h2)

question: How do environmental health challenges generally differ between urban and rural settings?

options.A: Rural areas are overcrowded while urban areas have vast open farmlands
options.B: Urban areas are completely free from any form of environmental hazards
options.C: Urban areas have more industrial pollution while rural areas face agricultural risks
options.D: Both settings experience identical levels of traffic congestion and smog

explanation: You got it! Cities deal with traffic and factories, while villages face challenges like farming chemicals or lack of clean water sources.

question: What does using the word AND do when searching an online database?

options.A: To automatically translate articles into English
options.B: To narrow your search by combining different concepts
options.C: To completely eliminate irrelevant foreign languages
options.D: To broaden your search by adding similar synonyms

explanation: Using AND tells the database to fetch articles containing all your search terms, which helps trim down a long list of results. You've got this!

question: Why is food safety especially important for individuals living with HIV?

options.A: Unsafe food stops the body from absorbing any vitamins
options.B: Contaminated food directly neutralizes antiretroviral medications
options.C: It prevents the sudden development of severe food allergies
options.D: Their weakened immune systems are more vulnerable to infections

explanation: Correct! Because the immune system may be compromised, patients can catch foodborne and waterborne illnesses much more easily.

question: Which imaging test is safest and most commonly used to look at a pregnant woman's kidneys?

options.A: Renal ultrasound
options.B: Magnetic resonance angiography
options.C: Computed tomography scan
options.D: Abdominal x-ray with contrast

explanation: Ultrasound uses safe sound waves instead of radiation, making it completely harmless for both mum and baby.

question: What is the correct way to dry nebulizer parts after washing them?

options.A: Air dry them completely on a clean paper towel or lint-free cloth
options.B: Blow hot air through them using a standard hair dryer on high heat
options.C: Place them inside a sealed plastic bag while they are still soaking wet
options.D: Wipe them dry using a heavily used cloth towel from the laundry bin

explanation: Air drying on a clean surface prevents germ transfer from dirty towels and ensures no moisture is trapped inside. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h8)

question: What is the main reason a patient experiences angina pectoris (chest pain)?

options.A: Inadequate oxygen supply to the heart muscle
options.B: Sudden electrical failure of the heart ventricles
options.C: Severe inflammation of the outer heart lining
options.D: Excessive fluid buildup inside the lung cavities

explanation: Think of the heart muscle as a busy engine—when it works harder than the oxygen supplied by narrowed blood vessels can support, it protests with chest pain (angina). You've got this!

question: When would a community health team rely on a sample survey instead of a census?

options.A: When recording a marriage certificate
options.B: When complete registration is not possible
options.C: When every single citizen comes to the clinic
options.D: When the government wants to count every building

explanation: Sample surveys are used to gather reliable estimates from a smaller group when tracking down every single person is too difficult. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h2)

question: Which secondary skin lesion looks like a narrow crack going down into the skin layer?

options.A: Fissure
options.B: Ulcer
options.C: Lichenification
options.D: Excoriation

explanation: Picture chapped lips or dry, cracked heels—that's a fissure. It's a sharp, linear crack in the skin.

question: Why can keeping professional boundaries sometimes be tricky in community nursing?

options.A: Community nurses are legally required to live with the families they care for.
options.B: Extended time spent in private homes can cause personal and professional lines to blur.
options.C: Hospital administrators force nurses to become close friends with patients.
options.D: Patients in communities never share personal stories with nurses.

explanation: Spending hours in someone's home feels cozy and personal, which makes it easy to forget professional boundaries. Staying mindful keeps everyone safe!

question: What is a major hurdle when trying to make national health policies work successfully in Nigeria?

options.A: Strict international bans on local medicine production
options.B: A total lack of written guidelines in government offices
options.C: Implementation gaps caused by funding and resource distribution issues
options.D: The absence of any trained healthcare workers in the entire country

explanation: Nigeria often has great written policies, but turning those plans into actual working services on the ground is tricky due to funding shortages and logistical challenges.

question: In midwifery, what does the term 'gravidity' mean?

options.A: The number of surgical deliveries performed
options.B: The total number of times a woman has been pregnant
options.C: The number of children currently living at home
options.D: The total weight of all babies delivered

explanation: Think of gravidity as the pregnancy counter! It counts every single time a woman has been pregnant, no matter how the pregnancy ended.

question: A patient scheduled for a barium enema says their lower belly is very painful and feels hard like a board. What should you do first as a nurse?

options.A: Proceed with the bowel cleansing enemas as originally planned
options.B: Give a strong oral laxative to speed up their prep
options.C: Hold the procedure and report these findings to the doctor immediately
options.D: Encourage the patient to drink extra water to flush out the bowel

explanation: A hard, painful abdomen can be a sign of a serious bowel emergency like a perforation. Always pause and report unusual findings right away.

question: A patient struggles with English, and her young son offers to translate for you. What is the best thing to do?

options.A: Use hand gestures instead of words to avoid needing any translation.
options.B: Accept the son's help immediately to save time on the ward.
options.C: Ask another nurse who is busy with medication to translate.
options.D: Request a certified medical interpreter to ensure accurate translation.

explanation: Correct! Certified interpreters keep things confidential and medically accurate, whereas family members might leave out important details.

question: Why is home health care such a big win for the Nigerian healthcare system?

options.A: It removes the need for trained nursing professionals
options.B: It helps decongest overcrowded tertiary hospitals
options.C: It guarantees uninterrupted electricity supply in every home
options.D: It completely eliminates the cost of medical supplies

explanation: True! Managing stable patients at home takes a huge load off our busy public hospitals.

question: What is the key sign of compartment syndrome that sets it apart from normal broken bone pain?

options.A: Mild aching pain that only occurs when the patient tries to walk
options.B: A gradual itching sensation underneath the plaster cast shell
options.C: Severe pain that is not relieved by standard opioid pain medications
options.D: Complete absence of any pain due to sudden nerve death

explanation: When pain is extreme and doesn't get better even with strong painkillers, think compartment syndrome! It means dangerous pressure is building up inside the muscle compartments.

question: Which mental ability tends to fade first in degenerative brain conditions?

options.A: Short-term memory
options.B: Long-term childhood memories
options.C: Basic emotional expression
options.D: The ability to hear sounds

explanation: Recent memories are usually affected long before older, deeply rooted childhood memories start to fade.

question: In which week of enteric fever is a blood culture most likely to give a positive result?

options.A: Fifth week
options.B: Sixth week
options.C: Third week
options.D: First week

explanation: Spot on! The bacteria is highest in the bloodstream right at the start of the illness, making the first week ideal for a blood culture.

question: What is the very first step a nurse must take before starting CPR on a fallen person?

options.A: Attach the automated external defibrillator
options.B: Ensure the surrounding scene is safe
options.C: Open the airway with a head-tilt maneuver
options.D: Check the patient for a pulse

explanation: Rescuers must check for hazards like fire, live wires, or traffic so they do not become victims themselves. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h3)

question: What are the two main components that make up human consciousness?

options.A: Memory and speech
options.B: Wakefulness and awareness
options.C: Sensation and movement
options.D: Reflexes and coordination

explanation: Consciousness is defined clinically by a person's physical wakefulness and their cognitive awareness of themselves and the environment. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T6#GNS222_U3_T6_h1)

question: What is the primary physical cause of obstetric fistula in young mothers?

options.A: Severe malnutrition during early childhood
options.B: A hereditary genetic blood disorder
options.C: Exposure to industrial chemical toxins
options.D: Prolonged and obstructed labor without timely surgical care

explanation: Obstetric fistula happens when labor gets stuck for too long without medical help. The constant pressure creates a tear or opening between the birth canal and the bladder or rectum. Timely medical care prevents this tragic injury.

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge facing nursing education updates in developing areas?

options.A: Resistance to change from traditional workers
options.B: An excess of state-of-the-art simulation equipment
options.C: Shortages of qualified academic teaching staff
options.D: Infrastructure deficits like erratic electricity

explanation: Correct! Schools usually suffer from a *lack* of modern equipment, not an excess of it.

question: What patient detail is usually written on an ADR form to protect their privacy?

options.A: National ID number
options.B: Home address
options.C: Initials
options.D: Full residential phone number

explanation: Using just the patient's initials keeps their identity confidential while still letting the clinical team trace the record if needed.

question: What do we mean by 'gender norms'?

options.A: Genetic markers inherited from parents
options.B: Medical guidelines for reproductive health
options.C: Fixed biological limits of the human body
options.D: Societal rules dictating expected behaviors

explanation: Great job! Gender norms are simply the unwritten rules or cultural standards that society uses to guide how men and women 'should' act.

question: How do heart valves get infected when bacteria temporarily enter the bloodstream?

options.A: Low blood pressure forces bacteria to settle inside the heart chambers.
options.B: Circulating bacteria stick to rough platelet-fibrin deposits on the injured valve lining.
options.C: Bacteria actively bore through healthy muscle tissue to reach the inner valves.
options.D: Infections start in the lungs and migrate directly through the coronary arteries.

explanation: When the inner lining of the heart is already roughened up, floating bacteria easily grab onto tiny tiny clots there and start multiplying.

question: What is a major challenge for nursing students facing heavy financial stress?

options.A: Elimination of the need to purchase nursing textbooks
options.B: An immediate increase in clinical ward placement scores
options.C: Free access to high-end medical simulation software
options.D: Balancing exhausting work schedules with studies, leaving little time for rest

explanation: Financial pressure often forces students to hustle outside of school, cutting deeply into study and recovery time. Hang in there—balancing nursing school is no small feat!

question: Why do patients who receive repeated blood transfusions end up with an overload of iron in their bodies?

options.A: Transfused red blood cells immediately break down in the digestive tract
options.B: The human body lacks an active physiological mechanism to excrete excess iron
options.C: Kidneys filter out red blood cells but trap all the iron in the nephrons
options.D: The liver actively manufactures iron whenever foreign blood is introduced

explanation: Our bodies are great at holding onto iron, but we have no natural way to get rid of extra amounts. Every transfusion adds more iron, which builds up over time.

question: A patient cannot afford expensive imported foods listed on a standard diet sheet. What should you do as their nurse?

options.A: Tell them to stop worrying about nutrition and just eat less food
options.B: Discharge the patient without any dietary plan
options.C: Suggest nutritious, affordable, and culturally familiar local food alternatives
options.D: Insist that they find extra money to buy the prescribed imported items

explanation: Great nursing judgment! Always adapt care to fit the patient's pocket by recommending budget-friendly, local Nigerian food options.

question: What is a normal and harmless effect of rifampin that nurses should warn patients about?

options.A: Bright green coloration of saliva and fingernails
options.B: Permanent yellow tinting of the skin and eye sclera
options.C: Orange-red discoloration of urine, sweat, and tears
options.D: Severe darkening of the skin on the hands and feet

explanation: Rifampin naturally dyes body fluids a reddish-orange color. It looks alarming, but it's completely normal and harmless!

question: Which part of the brain matures last during the teenage years, affecting self-control?

options.A: Limbic system
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Brainstem
options.D: Prefrontal cortex

explanation: You nailed it! The prefrontal cortex is our brain's planning and decision-making center, and it's one of the last areas to fully mature.

question: Why do patients with viral hepatitis turn yellow (jaundice)?

options.A: Excessive production of red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.B: Severe dehydration concentrating bile pigments in the skin
options.C: Damaged liver cells cannot process and clear out bilirubin
options.D: Direct bacterial infection of the superficial skin layers

explanation: When liver cells are inflamed, they struggle to process bilirubin properly. This yellow pigment builds up in the blood and skin, causing jaundice.

question: A patient asks how long an egg can survive and be fertilized after ovulation. What is your best response?

options.A: Up to 5 days
options.B: About 24 hours
options.C: Less than 1 hour
options.D: Exactly 1 week

explanation: Good clinical knowledge to have! An ovulated egg has a short window of about 12 to 24 hours to meet a sperm before it breaks down.

question: What is the main goal of a hormone suppression test?

options.A: To see if the body can lower hormone output when triggered
options.B: To replace missing hormones in a deficient patient
options.C: To destroy overactive endocrine tissue using high doses
options.D: To measure baseline hormone levels without any stress

explanation: Suppression tests check whether the body's natural brakes can shut down a gland. If hormone levels refuse to drop, hypersecretion is confirmed. You're mastering diagnostics step by step! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h4)

question: What clinical sign typically shows that a patient is slipping into the progressive stage of shock?

options.A: A sustained increase in urine output
options.B: Normal resting heart rate values
options.C: A sudden drop in blood pressure
options.D: Warm and flushed skin all over

explanation: You've got this! Early on, the body tries hard to compensate, but once blood pressure suddenly drops, it means those backup mechanisms are getting tired and failing to keep up.

question: How fast do the intense symptoms of a sudden gout attack usually peak?

options.A: Gradually across a full year
options.B: Within 12 to 24 hours
options.C: Right after finishing a heavy meal
options.D: Over several weeks to months

explanation: That's right! Gout attacks come on fast and furious, usually hitting their most painful peak within just half a day to a full day.

question: What is a key clinical marker used to evaluate the success of long-term diabetes management?

options.A: Hemoglobin A1c trends
options.B: Shoe size measurements
options.C: Frequency of dental visits
options.D: Hair color and texture

explanation: That's it! Tracking A1c over time gives a clear, reliable picture of how steady blood sugar levels have been.

question: A nurse notices a frayed electrical cord on an infusion pump. What is the immediate action to take?

options.A: Leave a sticky note on the screen and use it for one patient
options.B: Remove the pump from service and tag it for repair
options.C: Wrap the frayed area tightly with standard office tape
options.D: Plug it into a different wall socket to test the current

explanation: Frayed electrical cords pose severe shock and fire risks, so faulty equipment must be immediately taken out of use and labeled for biomedical maintenance. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h2)

question: What change in vital signs do you commonly notice in a physically distressed mum?

options.A: Fast heart rate and rapid breathing
options.B: High and bounding pulse pressure
options.C: Very low body temperature
options.D: Slow, shallow respiratory rate

explanation: That adrenaline rush speeds everything up! You'll often spot a racing heart (tachycardia) and quick, shallow breathing (tachypnea).
